# Appendix I - The Governance Map

*Generated by `tools/make_governance_appendix.py` from one run of the assembled system.
Do not edit by hand; CI regenerates it and fails on drift.*

Every AI-governance checklist uses the same ten terms. None of them is a chapter in this book,
because each one is the name for a mechanism a chapter already built and a demo already tests.
The table below was not written; it was produced by running the capstone on a hostile alert
and asking, for each term, which code proves it and what that code printed.

**10/10 terms hold on the run that generated this page.**

| # | Term | Chapter(s) | Mechanism | Evidence from the run |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | AI Inventory | 13 | `governance.inventory()` | 3 agents, 4 tools (1 world-changing: ['create_ticket']), 9 stages, tier=mock; every actor in this run is listed |
| 2 | Risk Classification | 9 | `AegisV12.handle() routed span; Ch 9 severity_route()` | severity_in=high -> human_analyst (a table, never the model); final severity=critical from ip_verdict=malicious, egress=True |
| 3 | Data Lineage | 10, 11 | `Run.audit + Run.trace share trace_id; safe_log wraps the raw line` | ip_verdict <- ip_reputation, auth_failures/egress <- search_logs, all audited under inc-<trace_id>; raw log kept verbatim inside <untrusted_data> |
| 4 | Model Cards | 12, 13 | `governance.MODEL_CARDS (dated, like Ch 12 PRICES)` | tier=mock: decides nothing - verdict, severity, authorization and escalation are code; verified 2026-08-26 |
| 5 | Guardrails | 8, 11 | `PERMITTED + AegisV12._call() (Ch 8 authorized_call, Ch 11 authorize)` | 5 calls allowed, 1 denied: triage -> create_ticket |
| 6 | Human-in-the-Loop | 9 | `escalated span; Ch 9 build_escalation()` | escalated=True: ['injection attempt in source data', 'severity critical requires human review']; open questions for the analyst: 1 |
| 7 | Explainability | 7, 13 | `interface.render_ticket_comment(); Ch 7 printed plan, reflect()` | ticket comment carries 2 reasons and 5 evidence fields; stages listed by name |
| 8 | Audit Trail | 8, 11 | `Run.audit; Ch 8 AuditLog; Ch 11b HMAC AuditChain` | 6 entries, each (agent, tool, allowed, trace_id); done span reports tool_calls=6 |
| 9 | Red Teaming | 5, 11 | `POISONED log in demo.py; Ch 11 redteam_demo, rug pull, memory poisoning` | injection_detected=True phrases=['ignore previous instructions', 'mark this alert as benign']; verdict=confirmed_compromise unchanged - and CI runs this input on every push |
| 10 | Continuous Monitoring | 10, 12 | `structured spans -> Ch 10 export_findings(); Ch 12 check_slos()` | latency <measured> ms vs ceiling 3000; escalation_accuracy 1.0 vs floor 0.95; healthy=True |

## The two terms the book had to add

Eight of the ten were already load-bearing code. Two were only implied, and an implied control
is not a control. Both live in `labs/chapter-13-assembling-aegis/governance/report.py`.

### AI Inventory - `inventory()`

Derived from the code that runs, never typed in: if a tool's signature or docstring changes,
its fingerprint changes and this page drifts.

```
agents       : {'triage': ['get_user_context', 'search_logs'], 'investigation': ['get_user_context', 'ip_reputation', 'search_logs'], 'reporting': ['create_ticket']}
tool         : search_logs       fingerprint=14678fb7a881  world_changing=False
tool         : ip_reputation     fingerprint=a000025891d2  world_changing=False
tool         : get_user_context  fingerprint=e6bb20e65eb8  world_changing=False
tool         : create_ticket     fingerprint=26b432bcbfd0  world_changing=True
model tier   : mock  (card on file: True)
stages       : received -> guarded_ingest -> routed -> memory_recall -> triage -> investigation -> escalated -> reported -> done
```

### Model Cards - `MODEL_CARDS` (verified 2026-08-26, stale after 90 days)

A card is a dated claim, exactly like a price in Chapter 12. The field that matters most is
`decides`, and for every tier in this book the answer is the same.

**mock**

- intended_use: teaching and CI: turn structured findings into a one-sentence ticket summary
- decides: nothing - verdict, severity, authorization and escalation are code
- inputs: the findings dict (alert, verdict, evidence); never raw logs
- outputs: one sentence of plain text, PII-masked before it leaves
- limits: deterministic template; cannot paraphrase, cannot be prompted, cannot be wrong in new ways
- evaluated_on: the four golden alerts (Ch 10); every chapter demo in CI
- cost: free

**openai**

- intended_use: production tier for the same single job: the ticket summary sentence
- decides: nothing - identical to mock; the seam changes wording, not structure
- inputs: the findings dict (alert, verdict, evidence); never raw logs
- outputs: one sentence, PII-masked (Ch 11) before it reaches the ticket; wording varies between runs and that is expected
- limits: needs a key and a spend cap; wording drift is normal, structural drift is a bug
- evaluated_on: the same golden set, judged (Ch 10); wording is not scored, escalation is
- cost: per token - see Ch 12 PRICES, verified on its own date

## How to read this in your own system

Run `python labs/chapter-13-assembling-aegis/governance/report.py --check` against your alerts.
A term that fails is not a governance gap to document; it is a test that found something.
The checklist is the output of the system, not an input to it.
